content:
When Apple launched the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out the most: the all-new Siri Recap feature, and a significantly improved heart rate monitor. While these two features were part of why I bought the new Apple Watch, I discovered there's far more to be delighted about than just these two.

Battery and charging

Although Apple's website doesn't list any additional battery life improvements for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, the battery life genuinely feels longer. As I've written before, before using the Apple Watch Series 12, I was a WHOOP user, and although I kept my Apple Watch, I never used it to track sleep.

After the launch event, I decided to give Apple Watch's sleep tracking a try. That said, on my Series 11, juggling sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a hassle. After wearing the watch all day, I had to top it up a bit before bed, then charge it again when I woke up.

On the Series 12, the situation is different. It has enough battery to last a full day and a full night, so I now only charge it when I wake up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges noticeably faster, making charging far less of a chore. According to Apple, just 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 12 hours of use.

I suspect the all-new S11 chip (derived from the A20 Pro's 2nm design) is one of the main reasons for the perceived significant improvement in battery life. Whatever the reason, it's genuinely refreshing not to worry about battery for sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12. Another major advantage of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 feels much faster, especially when using Siri.

Software exclusives

On the Series 12, Apple has finally added a proper pedometer as a complication, which I enjoy viewing in the Smart Stack. Will this feature trickle down to older Apple Watches? Quite likely. After all, Apple has been counting steps all along. The Apple Watch Series 12 certainly counts steps more accurately, but given that the data has always existed, I think Apple should have added this complication directly. Regardless, having this feature on the Series 12 is a good thing.

Another interesting new feature is the entire Readiness app, which gives you an idea of how your body is doing today based on your sleep last night, your activity the day before, and your vitals. This is similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm of course delighted that Apple has brought it to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, this feature is exclusive to the Series 12, but given Apple's reluctance to calculate with less accurate data, I can understand why.

Verdict

All in all, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a pretty solid upgrade. It's a typical 'S' year upgrade, but if you care about your Apple Watch actually doing more rather than just looking different, I'd say this might be the most substantial year-over-year improvement since the Apple Watch Series 4.

The bezels are indeed slightly thicker than on the Series 10 and 11. As someone who uses a black-background watch face, I can't say I've noticed it much — though I'd expect Apple to improve this in the next generation.

One last thing worth mentioning: the Apple Watch Series 12 brings Ceramic Shield 2 to the aluminium models, making them far more scratch-resistant than any previous Apple Watch. Although I haven't owned it long enough to truly test this, so far my Apple Watch remains as good as new.

My favourite Apple accessory recommendations:

  • Anker Ultra-Slim MagSafe Battery
  • AirPods Pro 3 (twice the active noise cancellation performance of the AirPods Pro 2!)
  • Anker Nano 45W Smart Display Fast Charger
  • Anker Prime 25W 3-in-1 Portable MagSafe Charger
  • Logitech MX Master 4 for Mac Mouse
  • AirTag 2 4-pack (50% improved Precision Finding!)
  • Belkin iPhone MagSafe 3-in-1 Charging Stand
  • MOFT iPhone MagSafe Stand Wallet
